proposed.text: How long does copyright protection for architectural works extend under RA 8293?

options.text: For 20 years from the date the design is first created and registered with the Intellectual Property Office
For the lifetime of the architect plus 50 years after the architect's death
For 50 years from the date the building is completed and granted a certificate of occupancy
Only for 10 years unless the building remains in continuous use and the architect renews registration

rationale.c: This measures from building completion instead of the author's death.
rationale.d: This invents a short renewable term tied to continued building use.
rationale.correct: RA 8293 Section 213.1 protects works under Sections 172 and 173 during the life of the author and for fifty years after death. For an individual architect's architectural work, the exam-safe term is lifetime plus 50 years after death, not 70 years and not a term measured from registration, completion, or occupancy.
rationale.takeaway: For individual architects, Section 213.1 uses life of the author plus 50 years.
